question.leadin: Descendents of convicts known as "currency lads" carried out raids on feral horses called brumbies in the bush and this region.
question.text: Name this region where jackaroos established "cattle empires" around stations. The disastrous Emu War occurred in this rural region of central Australia.
question.clue: An overland telegraph line through this region was scouted by Robert Burke and William Wills but was eventually built through Alice Springs.

swap.text: In 1932, this country sent soldiers to curb their pestilent emu population in the Emu War. This country, whose capital is Canberra ["can-burra"], now uses massive barrier fences to keep dingos away from farmland.
swap.clue: This country's longest serving prime minister was Robert Menzies, who founded its Liberal Party and famously called the middle class, "The Forgotten People".

question.text: This is the collective name given to Aboriginals who were taken from their families and forced to assimilate into white society. In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to this group.
question.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

swap.leadin: In order to pass otherwise deadlocked legislation, this party called its country's only-ever joint sitting of Parliament in 1974.
swap.text: Name this party. Australia's 1975 constitutional crisis was caused by John Kerr's dismissal of a Prime Minister of this party, Gough Whitlam, after the Liberal-National Coalition blocked supply to this left-wing party's government.
swap.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the only successful armed uprising in Australian history.
question.text: Major George Johnston invaded Government House and placed Bligh under arrest in this capital city of New South Wales.
question.clue: Lachlan Macquarie ("LACK-lan muh-KWAIR-ee") was placed in charge of this city after John Macarthur overthrew governor William Bligh in the Rum Rebellion.

swap.text: Unfortunately for him, Disraeli wouldn't be prime minister forever, especially after his retired rival William Gladstone led the Midlothian Campaign against him which helped this party retake parliament.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party (do NOT accept or prompt on “Labour” as this that did not exist yet)
swap.clue: A faction led by Robert Peel's followers combined with the Whigs to form this party, whose members included Herbert Asquith.

question.leadin: This group of eleven ships departed from Portsmouth, England in 1787.
question.text: Name this group of ships, which was under the command Arthur Phillip. They probably brought smallpox to the local population after landing in Botany Bay.
question.clue: This alliteratively named group of convicts and colonists that arrived in Botany Bay in 1788.

swap.text: Australian and New Zealander forces were joined in this unit. This unit notably fought in World War I and names the national day of remembrance in those two countries, celebrated on April 25.
swap.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This Australian prime minister began dismantling White Australia in 1966, a year before his mysterious disappearance during a swimming incident while in office.
question.clue: One ruler of this name allied with Tostig to fight against another ruler with this name at Stamford Bridge.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about penal colonies.
swap.text: The First Fleet, under the command of Arthur Phillip, established a prison colony in this Australian state. Sydney is located in this present-day state.
swap.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

question.leadin: In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to the Stolen Generation, who were children of these people that were forcibly taken from their families.
question.text: Name these indigenous people of Australia.
question.clue: Many of these people were taken from their families and integrated into white culture, becoming the Stolen Generation.

swap.text: William Bligh was overthrown as Governor of New South Wales in this rebellion, which resulted from his attempts to curtail trade of its namesake liquor. This rebellion was led by John Macarthur and George Johnston.
swap.clue: Others associated with this event included John Blaxland and Richard Atkins, and it saw resistance along the after the storming of the Government House.

question.leadin: A key controversy in the history wars is over whether the separation of families from children described by this adjective constitutes genocide.
question.text: Give the adjective commonly used to describe those "generations" of children, the subjects of the report Bringing Them Home.

swap.leadin: This party took office under Malcolm Fraser after governor-general John Kerr controversially ousted Gough ("goff") Whitlam in 1975.
swap.text: Name this party, which made extensive spending cuts after succeeding the Keating government. During the 1970s, this party began a coalition arrangement with the National Country Party.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Australia [or LPA; accept word forms like Australian Liberal Party or Australians Liberals; prompt on Liberal Party and ask “of what country”; don’t accept ALP]
swap.clue: This party regained power after the Loans Affair presaged ("PRESS-idged") the collapse of Gough Whitlam's ("goff WIT-lum's") government.

question.leadin: Answer the following about prime ministers of Australia.
question.text: This Australian prime minister used the slogan "All the way with LBJ" to increase Australian involvement in the Vietnam War, but he is most famous for disappearing at Cheviot Beach in 1967.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.text: Kelly was captured in a shootout with police in this town in Victoria.
swap.clue: The shootout where Kelly was captured occurred in this small town in Northeast Victoria. A plan to derail train carrying policemen was foiled by the efforts of hostage Thomas Curnow.

question.text: This Australian Labor Party PM's foreign minister Gareth Evans claimed the Santa Cruz massacre was merely an "aberration." This personal friend of Suharto served as PM from 1991 to '96.

swap.leadin: A famous cartoon of this event depicts the Governor of the territory in which it took place cowering under his bed.
swap.text: Name this uprising, led by George Macarthur. Macarthur was angered by, among other things, a lien against one of his ships for abetting an escaped convict and Major George Johnston.
swap.clue: This rebellion took place after the arrest of John Macarthur, a lieutenant of the New South Wales Corp. It was named for the nickname of the New South Wales Corp, which had to do with a product the Corp traded.

question.leadin: Answer the following about gold rushes in Australia and New Zealand during the mid-1800s.
question.text: This man led the gold miners at the Battle of the Eureka Stockade and parlayed his subsequent fame into a long political career, rising all the way to Speaker of the Victorian Legislative Assembly.

swap.leadin: Name these locations that appear in the Holmes canon.
swap.text: In "The Boscombe Valley Mystery," the last words of Charles McCarthy are interpreted by Holmes to refer to the name of this city. This boomtown of the Australian gold rush was the site of the Eureka Stockade.
